scope: Read-only build and frozen-profile diagnosis. Created after the R22 long-graph collection; it is not part of that collection freeze and contains no timing coefficient or target-LLM latency.

fixed_runtime_dll.role: R22 synthetic probe actual loaded CUDA DLL and current/cta_issue frozen native runtime CUDA DLL
fixed_runtime_dll.identity_conclusion: same SHA256 across R22, current and cta_issue: fixed native CUDA DLL identity matches; no LLM timing was read.

compile_command_token_checks.conclusion: USE_CUDA_GRAPH cannot be defined by common.cuh from this recorded ggml-cuda compile command because none of the enabling graph macros is present.

source_conditions.condition: USE_CUDA_GRAPH is defined only by GGML_CUDA_USE_GRAPHS, GGML_HIP_GRAPHS or GGML_MUSA_GRAPHS.
Even compiled graph support is disabled by GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS environment presence or pre-Volta architecture.
MUL_MAT_ID paths that require stream synchronization make a graph incompatible.
first-node graph key, graph uid and copied tensor/node properties determine update/stability.
capture needs graph support, eligibility, then two stable calls; changed properties reset warmup.
capture/end/instantiate/update/replay APIs execute only in USE_CUDA_GRAPH branch.

protocol_environment.GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS: explicitly null/unset in r2 protocol; build-time disabled support is the decisive condition

import_table_observation.conclusion: The fixed DLL imports per-kernel launch APIs but no CUDA Graph APIs. This independently agrees with the build macro test and R22 CUPTI per-node cudaLaunchKernelExC observations.

build_scope.conclusion: For the fixed DLL, CUDA Graph replay was compiled out. Do not attribute R22 per-node launches to WDDM, graph-shape instability, or runtime warmup failure.

profile_lineage.base_profile: build_matching_scenario calls build_reference_scenario; frozen reference GPU profile supplies kernel_launch_ns=1000.0, launch_resource_id=gpu0.frontend.
profile_lineage.frequency_change_only: predict_cell replaces tensor_core.frequency_ghz from frozen clock but does not replace kernel_launch_ns.
profile_lineage.launch_calibration: both freezes declare calibration_applied=false. Frozen calibration code replaces GPU kernel_launch_ns only when explicit apply_launch and a launch profile are both present; that path is not active here.
profile_lineage.graph_replay_metadata: predict_cell writes compiled_cuda_graphs from frozen config and cuda_graph_replay_cost_applied=false.

charging_path.base: Generic GPU cost models append a kernel_launch CostPhase with ResourceDemand(gpu.launch_resource_id, gpu.kernel_launch_ns).
charging_path.planner: _lower_tensor_operation turns each cost phase into a TaskSpec. It defaults emit_kernel_launch=true and only overrides a kernel-launch phase when an explicit phase launch calibration exists.
charging_path.current_interpretation: The 1000ns amount is a GPU frontend resource demand attached to modeled cost phases, not a host resource and not a pure unowned additive constant.
charging_path.physicality_limit: This frozen path has no mapped native kernel ledger demonstrating one modeled launch phase equals one physical CUDA launch for every semantic operator. Limited fusion can reduce cost through eliminated_launches*kernel_launch_ns, but that is a planner decision, not R22-derived physical-kernel proof.

double_count_or_gap_evidence.finding: No active CUDA Graph replay charge in current/cta_issue
double_count_or_gap_evidence.evidence: All frozen configs set compiled_cuda_graphs=false and predictor metadata sets cuda_graph_replay_cost_applied=false.

double_count_or_gap_evidence.finding: InvocationLifecycle exists but is not production-wired in frozen source
double_count_or_gap_evidence.evidence: Only invocation.py and unit tests reference InvocationLifecycle/InvocationOverheads; no production caller was found in frozen current/cta_issue source.

InvocationLifecycle would add capture/update/launch/synchronize tasks while generic cost phases already add per-operator kernel_launch tasks. A replay integration must suppress/rewrite per-op launch phases within the same physical graph invocation.
Conversely, replacing all per-op phases with one invocation launch would under-count R22-style eager paths, which observed 64 or 256 cudaLaunchKernelExC calls per formal graph.

control_plane_planner computes fusion_credit_ns as eliminated_launches*profile.kernel_launch_ns. It has no source-qualified CUDA Graph state, so it must remain separate from capture/replay eligibility.

next_mechanism_requirements: Add a source-qualified dispatch mode per physical invocation: eager_per_node, graph_capture, graph_update_or_recapture, graph_replay, or unsupported.
Require build macro, effective environment, GPU CC, compatibility blockers, graph key/uid, node-property stability, warmup and graph-instance state before selecting a graph mode.
Create a physical launch ledger that maps modeled operator phases to observed/evidenced launch cardinality; do not infer one semantic operation equals one CUDA kernel.
Make launch ownership exclusive: eager uses per-physical-launch frontend demand; replay uses one graph-launch demand plus capture/update transition costs; never charge both for the same invocation.
Keep final synchronization separately modeled and do not derive a CPU constant from host wall minus kernel-only timing.
